title: An item whose verdict is persistently malformed does not take a triage slot on every run
actual: In apply mode a failed item gets no label and is not recorded, so it stays first in the todo list; with TRIAGE_MAX_ITEMS=2 and two such items, three runs judge items 1 and 2 six times (paid each time) and item 3 never.
expected: A failed item is remembered (like dry-judged / handler-failed) and retried later or after the others, so newer items are still triaged and the same bad answer is not paid for every 4 hours.
why_it_matters: #205 stopped the abort but left the retry-and-pay-first behaviour: a few hostile or odd issues block all later triage.

title: A failed label edit after the triage comment does not make the next run comment again
actual: Labels are added with check=False after the comment is posted. If the 'triaged' edit fails, nothing is noticed; the item still lacks 'triaged' and the next run posts a second full comment (repro: 2 comments over two runs).
expected: The item is not answered twice: a failed 'triaged' label is detected and retried without a new comment (or the daemon recognises its own marker comment on the thread).
why_it_matters: #206 fixed only the comment-fails case; the inverse transient error produces duplicate public comments every 4 hours until a label edit succeeds.

title: A transient GitHub error while filing a feedback ticket leaves the comment to be retried, not silently dropped
actual: The comment id is written to feedback-seen.json before post_feedback runs. When `gh issue create` fails with HTTP 502 nothing was filed or answered, yet the next run reports 0 new comments: the user's report is never ticketed or answered.
expected: The comment is marked done only once the ticket exists (or the failure happened after it was created); a failure before creation is retried on the next run.
why_it_matters: The #206 fix trades a duplicate ticket for a permanently lost one, with only a log line as trace.

title: A verdict with duplicate_of: true is refused instead of posted as '#True'
actual: isinstance(True, int) and True in {1, 2}: the verdict is accepted, labelled duplicate, and the comment says 'This looks like a duplicate of #True'.
expected: ValueError: duplicate_of must be an integer item number (bool excluded); same in validate_feedback.
why_it_matters: The validator is the boundary between model output and what is posted; a type confusion gets through it.

title: A draft-pr issue can be retried after its first attempt pushed the branch but failed to open the PR
actual: #207 resets the local branch with checkout -B, but the earlier attempt already pushed auto/N-slug; the retry pushes a new commit without --force and git rejects it (non-fast-forward), so the item fails again, every time.
expected: The retry opens the draft PR: push with --force-with-lease to the daemon's own auto/ branch, or reuse/delete the remote branch first.
why_it_matters: #207's stated outcome (a draft-pr issue can be retried) is not met for the common transient failure of `gh pr create` after a successful push.

title: A hanging test in the sandbox fails its item instead of aborting the whole handle run
actual: sandboxed() runs with timeout=1800; subprocess.TimeoutExpired is not in cmd_handle's except tuple, so it propagates, the run stops, the item is not marked handler-failed and is the first one retried (and re-paid) by every later run.
expected: TimeoutExpired is turned into RuntimeError (or caught) so the item is marked handler-failed and the next item is handled.
why_it_matters: Agent- or outsider-written code controls whether tests hang, so one crafted issue can wedge the handler permanently; the same class of abort #205 set out to remove.

title: With TRIAGE_REPO set, the tree the agent reads to triage, plan and answer feedback is that repository's main
actual: #208 moved review/draft fetches to REPO_URL, but update_tree() still adds the worktree at and fetches from the git remote `origin` of the checkout the script is in; triage, feedback and plan runs (claude(..., TREE, READ_ONLY)) read that code while gh comments on TRIAGE_REPO.
expected: update_tree fetches REPO_URL main (as handle_draft_pr already does) so every agent run sees the code of the repository it is judging.
why_it_matters: Verdicts such as 'valid bug' or 'already fixed' and plans are written against another repository's code.

title: A suite failure that appears only after the agent's own test is not scored as green by the flaky rule
actual: run_suite re-runs the failed test ids alone; a test broken by in-process state the agent's new test leaks passes alone, is recorded as 'flaky' and suite_pass becomes True (repro: 1 failed, 1 passed in the full run, suite_pass True).
expected: Only a failure that also disappears when the whole suite is run again counts as flaky; a failure that reproduces in the full-suite order stays red (re-run the full suite, or run the failed tests in their original order with their predecessors).
why_it_matters: #260 made a red suite caused by the agent's change score green, which biases the release table's suite column and the acceptance of every arm.

title: A run cut off by the timeout is not recorded with zero cost and zero context
actual: With no `result` event (5400 s timeout), transcript() returns cost 0 and ctx_tokens 0 although 40 assistant messages used 2M cached input tokens; per_run feeds these zeros into the release table means.
expected: Cost and context are estimated from the per-message usage (or the run is flagged and excluded from cost/context means).
why_it_matters: The slowest, most expensive runs are the ones that time out; they lower the arm's average cost and context, so the release table's 'cost -N%' is computed wrongly.

title: The release table uses the devkb navigation counts stored in the results when the transcript is not under bench/policy/runs
actual: counts() re-reads B/runs/<run>/stream.jsonl and returns (0,0,0) when it is missing, ignoring the row's devkb_nav / devkb_selftest (remeasure.py has --runs DIRs because transcripts live elsewhere); the table shows nav 0 and self-tests 0 for a run whose row says 7 and 2.
expected: Fall back to the row's stored devkb_nav, devkb_selftest (and say when neither exists) instead of printing 0.
why_it_matters: 'devkb nav' and 'self-tests' are the columns #258 introduced; a results file moved to another machine silently reports that devkb was not used.

title: A run refused for a red base is run again after the base is fixed
actual: _run_one skips any run whose end file exists unless exit == 'error'; 'base-red' is skipped, so after the red base is fixed `policybench.py run` prints 'skip' and the arm stays empty (score prints REFUSED).
expected: base-red ends are re-run like error ends (the setup is what failed, not the agent).
why_it_matters: #221's refusal is only useful if the batch can be completed after the fix; today the user must find and delete runs/<tag>/end by hand and may publish a table with a missing arm.

title: Re-scoring one arm keeps the other arms' rows in results-ISSUE.jsonl
actual: With POLICY_ARMS=after, score() skips the other arms and then rewrites results-ISSUE.jsonl and results-policy.jsonl from the rows it collected: the before arm's scored runs disappear from the files release_table.py reads.
expected: Rows of arms outside the filter are carried over from the saved score.json (or the existing file), so the release table input stays complete.
why_it_matters: A routine partial re-score silently produces a table with missing arms and no 'vs no devkb' column.
